rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 05 Oct 2028 (697 days left). This counts 2 years from 05 Oct 2026 (your purchase date - counted from the earliest possible day, to be safe). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 3,200, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with no filing fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

answer.summary: You bought a mixer online for 3200 rupees on 5 Oct 2026 and returned it on 8 Oct 2026 because it was broken. You did not get your money back.

claims.text: You are a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 because you bought goods for personal use and not for resale or commercial purpose.
A broken mixer is a defect under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
Refusing to take back defective goods and refund the money within 30 days is an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
Because you paid 3200 rupees, you must file your complaint in the District Consumer Commission, and there is no filing fee.
You have 697 days left to file your consumer complaint before the 5 Oct 2028 deadline.

next_steps.action: Call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
next_steps.why: This is a free first step to try and get your refund without going to court.

next_steps.action: File a written complaint to the online platform's grievance officer or customer care.
next_steps.why: This creates a record that you tried to resolve the issue directly.

next_steps.action: File an online complaint at e-jagriti.gov.in.
next_steps.why: This starts your official consumer case in the District Commission with no fee.

support.text: You are a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 because you bought goods for personal use and not for resale or commercial purpose.
support.reason: The law text defines 'consumer' as someone who buys goods for consideration, explicitly excludes those who obtain goods for resale or commercial purpose, and the sentence correctly applies this rule to the user's facts (personal use, not for resale or commercial purpose).

support.text: A broken mixer is a defect under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
support.reason: The law text defines 'defect' as any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in quality, and a broken mixer constitutes a fault/imperfection in the product.

support.text: Refusing to take back defective goods and refund the money within 30 days is an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
support.reason: The law text explicitly defines 'unfair trade practice' to include 'refusing, after selling goods... to take back or withdraw defective goods... and to refund the consideration thereof... within... thirty days', which directly matches the sentence.

support.text: Because you paid 3200 rupees, you must file your complaint in the District Consumer Commission, and there is no filing fee.
support.reason: The law text [CPJR2021_pecuniary] states District Commission has jurisdiction for consideration paid 'up to Rs 50 lakh', and while Rs 3200 falls within this, the text says nothing about filing fees. The sentence adds a 'no filing fee' condition that is not in this law text. (Note: The filing fee rule appears in a different cited law text [CPFEE_r7] which has a different threshold structure.)

support.text: Because you paid 3200 rupees, you must file your complaint in the District Consumer Commission, and there is no filing fee.
support.reason: The law text [CPFEE_r7] states 'No fee where the consideration paid is up to Rs 5 lakh.' Since Rs 3200 is up to Rs 5 lakh, there is no fee, and the sentence correctly applies this to the amount paid.

support.text: You have 697 days left to file your consumer complaint before the 5 Oct 2028 deadline.
support.reason: The law text [CPA2019_s69] states the complaint must be filed within two years from the date the cause of action arose, with possible condonation of delay for sufficient cause. It does not state a fixed '5 Oct 2028 deadline' nor calculate '697 days left' from any such date. The sentence adds a specific deadline date and day calculation that is not in the law text.

rendered.summary: Aapne 5 Oct 2026 ko online ₹3200 mein ek mixer kharida tha aur 8 Oct 2026 ko use wapas kar diya kyunki woh toota hua tha, lekin aapko aapke paise wapas nahi mile.
claims: Aap Consumer Protection Act, 2019 ke tehat ek consumer hain kyunki aapne saaman personal use ke liye kharida tha, resale ya commercial purpose ke liye nahi.
Ek toota hua mixer Consumer Protection Act, 2019 ke tehat ek defect hai.
Defective saaman ko wapas lene aur 30 din ke andar paise refund karne se mana karna Consumer Protection Act, 2019 ke tehat ek unfair trade practice hai.
Kyunki aapne ₹3200 pay kiye the, aapko apni complaint District Consumer Commission mein file karni hi chahiye, aur iski koi filing fee nahi hai.
5 Oct 2028 ki deadline se pehle apni consumer complaint file karne ke liye aapke paas 697 din bache hain.
next_steps: National Consumer Helpline par 1915 par call karein ya 8800001915 par WhatsApp karein. — Court jaye bina apna refund paane ki koshish karne ke liye yeh ek free pehla step hai.
Online platform ke grievance officer ya customer care ko ek written complaint file karein. — Isse ek record ban jata hai ki aapne issue ko directly resolve karne ki koshish ki thi.
e-jagriti.gov.in par ek online complaint file karein. — Isse District Commission mein aapka official consumer case shuru ho jata hai aur koi fee nahi lagti.

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
